answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake of quartz-backed credit that is slashed on fraud, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real money instead of being free. Reputation then accrues slowly over a long horizon of verified work, and new identities start with velvet-glove limits: tiny transaction caps that only grow after consistent honest behavior, making mass fake identities unprofitable before they can do damage.
